section_summary.extract_value: This section describes statistical analyses for the BAS-2: a principal-axis EFA with quartimax rotation was performed (with eigenvalues >1, scree plot, and parallel analysis used for retention) and the EFA was conducted separately for women and men. Ten independent t-tests compared BAS-2 items between genders, an additional t-test compared total BAS-2 scores, and Pearson correlations were used to examine associations among body appreciation, self-esteem, life satisfaction, BMI, and age. No explicit study numbering, sample sizes, demographic details, or BMI assessment methods are reported in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: The factor structure of the BAS-2 was examined using a principal-axis exploratory factor analysis (EFA) with quartimax rotation (...) The EFA was conducted separately for women and men. Ten independent ttests were used to compare BAS-2 items between men and women. Moreover, another independent-samples t-test was performed to compare the total score of BAS-2 between men and women. Pearson correlation coefficients were used to investigate associations between body appreciation, self-esteem, life satisfaction, BMI, and age.
